To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(i) task goals, (ii) location probability learning, and (iii) reward-based learning differentially guide spatial attention.

(i) task goals exert the strongest influence on spatial attention, (ii) location probability learning produces a smaller though still substantial effect on spatial attention, and (iii) reward learning has a negligible effect on spatial attention.
(1) goal-driven attention, (2) location probability cuing and (3) monetary reward all guide spatial attention.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how the brain allocates attention to different parts of the visual scene.
the role of attention in the perception of visual stimuli.
the mechanisms that guide attention in the visual search task, and the relative importance of task goals, statistical learning and monetary reward in the guidance of attention.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the strongest attentional guidance comes from goals, followed by statistical learning, and then reward.
goals, statistical learning and reward all have a role to play in directing spatial attention, with goals having the most powerful influence.
task goals, statistical learning and reward all modulate spatial attention.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the goal-driven attention is the strongest, followed by the location probability learning and reward learning.
task goals, visual statistics and reward are all capable of modulating spatial attention, but their relative strengths depend on how they are acquired and the context of task goals.
goals are the strongest driver of attention, followed by search habits and then priming.
The main takeaway from our work is that
goals, not rewards, guide spatial attention.
goals and statistical learning can be powerful and independent drivers of spatial attention.
task goals are the dominant driver of spatial attention.
